one_line_contribution: Instead of the single 'with the memory back' number that internalization papers report, measure the whole retrieval dose ladder (k=0,1,3,7, plus token-matched decoys) before and after memory-free internalization on ALFWorld/Qwen3-32B, and claim a specific shape -- the first retrieved item keeps roughly its pre-training value while items 2-7 lose theirs -- from which follows a token-optimal deployment at student+k=1 (~140 injected tokens) rather than memory-free or base+k=7 (~1,010 tokens).
closest_prior_work: SESA (arXiv:2607.29468, verified via the literature command, 2026-07-31): its own summary says evolving skill memory 'changes policy learning and the future training distribution while retaining value as optional external memory' -- i.e. it already reports the qualitative result that after internalization the bank still adds something (+0.5-1.0). It does not kill the proposal because it reports one dose in a QA/search domain with no seeds and no token axis; the proposal's increment is the *shape* across k and the iso-token point. Second threat, and the one the proposal underrates: Skill0.5 (arXiv:2605.28424, verified) is explicitly 'Joint Skill Internalization and Utilization', i.e. it already operationalizes the hybrid (some skills to weights, some kept in the prompt) and reports both arms -- so 'the hybrid, not the memory-free student, is best' is not itself new; only the dose-resolved, cost-matched version of it is. Third: Retrieval-Augmented LLM Agents (arXiv:2603.18272, verified, cit 5) establishes retrieval-aware fine-tuning as the standard trained-with-retrieval recipe, which is exactly the proposal's E6 arm demoted to a single-seed secondary. Also worth citing and absent: 'Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work--Until They Don't' (arXiv:2608.14036, 2026-08-14, found by my query 2) argues skills help by 'procedural anchoring... rather than injecting missing knowledge' -- essentially the proposal's cue-vs-procedure mechanism, already stated in the literature.
strongest_objection: P2, the headline half of the claim, is underpowered by construction from the proposal's own numbers, and Gate 0 does not fix it. P2 asks whether the student's k=1->k=7 slope is <=1/3 of the base's (confirm) or >=2/3 (falsify). Measurement A puts the base k=1->k=7 slope at +10.7 (seen) / +10.1 (unseen) net with the *full* 1,465-item bank; bank B is 30 % of the pool, so it will be smaller, and Gate 0 admits anything >=6. The band separating confirmation from falsification is therefore (2/3 - 1/3) x base slope = 3.4 net points at the measured full-bank value and 2.0 at the gate floor -- both well inside the proposal's own stated minimum detectable slope difference of ~5 net points (494 tasks x 3 seeds). So on the plan as written the study will very likely return a student slope that is statistically compatible with both 1/3x and 2/3x, and the pre-registration will have to declare P2 untestable after the confirmatory run rather than before. Compounding this: the shape is confounded with ceiling. Base k=7 is already 0.846/0.877; a student whose memory-free k=0 lands anywhere near 0.75-0.80 (plausible if context distillation retains the ~65 % Experience Distillation reports) has only ~8-12 points of headroom left, so a collapsed k=1->k=7 slope is arithmetically forced and says nothing about internalization. P1 and P2 in fact pull against each other -- P1 needs a *large* residual first-item gain (>=10 net points, i.e. the student did not internalize much), P2 needs the rest flat -- so 'the shape' may be no more than a re-description of where the student's k=0 happened to land, which is not a property of internalization at all.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Re-derive Gate 0 from the discrimination requirement rather than from a bare slope floor: require base_slope(k=1->k=7) on bank B such that (2/3 - 1/3) x base_slope exceeds the MDE, i.e. >=15 net points at the current +/-5 resolution -- and if the measured bank cannot deliver that, either widen the ladder (k=15), degrade the base (8B, or a harder/lower-ceiling split, or fewer max steps) to open headroom, or state up front that the study reports P1/P3 only. (2) Remove the ceiling confound by making the estimand headroom-normalized -- report each dose step as the fraction of remaining error closed, not raw net points -- and pre-register the shape claim on that scale; a raw-point slope ratio at 0.85 accuracy is not interpretable. (3) Add the k=0-matched control below. (4) Promote the retrieval-aware-SFT/memory-in-the-loop arm from 1 LoRA seed to the same 2-3 seeds as the core arms, since P7 is stated as a directional claim about slope ratios and one seed cannot support it. (5) Cite and differentiate from 2608.14036 (procedural anchoring) and Skill0.5's joint-internalization-and-utilization framing, which already own the mechanism story and the hybrid conclusion respectively.
missing_baseline: A k=0-matched (accuracy-matched origin) control for the dose ladder. Every slope contrast in the plan compares the student's ladder to the base's ladder from different starting accuracies, so a flatter student slope is inseparable from a higher origin and less headroom. The plan needs at least one base-side arm placed at the student's memory-free accuracy -- e.g. base+k=1 (or base+k=3) taken as the ladder origin and stepped to k=3/k=7 against student k=0 stepped to k=1/k=3, and/or an accuracy-matched weaker/stronger backbone -- so that 'the second item stopped paying' can be attributed to internalization rather than to sitting further up the same saturating curve. Secondarily, the named published trained-with-retrieval baseline (retrieval-augmented SFT, 2603.18272) appears only as a 1-seed secondary arm, yet it is the natural competitor on the token-accuracy frontier that P3 claims.
preprint_collision: No verified collision. The proposal's own check is one of the better ones I have seen in this round: four queries, each reported with returned IDs, dates and a stated reason for non-collision, and it names its channel limits honestly (S2+HF, --recent, WebSearch quota exhausted). I verified with `paper <id>` every arXiv ID the novelty argument leans on, and all resolved with the claimed content: 2607.29468 SESA (2026-07-31, 'retaining value as optional external memory'), 2603.18272 Retrieval-Augmented LLM Agents / retrieval-aware fine-tuning (2026-03-18, cit 5), 2607.21051 Sample-Efficient Learning from Agent Experience / Experience Distillation (2026-07-23), 2608.12218 Information Abundance Paradox (2026-08-12, cit 2), 2505.01812 New News (2025-05-03), 2608.15008 Harness the Memory substrate benchmark (2026-08-15), 2607.01480 Procedural Memory Distillation (2026-07-01), 2605.28424 Skill0.5 (2026-05-27), 2606.29502 UCOB (2026-07-17). I could not independently verify 2604.02268 (SKILL0) beyond its appearance in a search listing, and I did not check the archived internal ideas. My own searches, all answered by the literature command (S2+HF); WebSearch unavailable in this session, WebFetch never used: (1) 'dose-response of retrieved in-context experience after internalization: does retrieval still help a fine-tuned agent' --recent -> 2607.28272 MemHarness, 2607.10608 Compliance Trap, 2606.22844 RaMem, 2605.12493 LongMemEval-V2, 2605.10268 MemReread + off-topic hits; none traces accuracy across k after training. (2) 'is retrieved memory still additive after skill internalization: memory-free student re-given the bank at inference' --recent -> 2608.14036 Demystifying Agent Skills, 2607.29468 SESA, 2606.29502 UCOB, 2606.08755, 2604.02268 SKILL0, 2510.08564; the closest, 2608.14036, makes the procedural-anchoring mechanism claim but has no weights arm and no dose ladder. (3) 'number of in-context demonstrations k ablation after fine-tuning: diminishing marginal value of extra examples for a trained model' --recent -> only 2507.01679, 2506.04579, 2503.08640 (many-shot ICL selection/efficiency); empty on the actual question. (4) 'token cost accuracy Pareto frontier: fine-tuned agent with fewer retrieved memories versus untrained agent with many' --recent -> 2606.19919, 2606.07074 SlimSearcher, 2604.22750, 2602.13407, 2602.03073, 2601.19739, 2601.14192, 2510.01123; all efficiency-of-generation work, nothing on an injected-token frontier between substrates -- this is the emptiest and most favourable result for the proposal. (5) 'training with retrieved memory in the prompt makes the policy rely on it: context reliance crutch after fine-tuning LLM agents' --recent -> 2607.21106 AttriMem, 2606.22844, 2606.04536 Scaling Self-Evolving Agents via Parametric Memory, 2606.03197 MemTrain, 2605.30690 ElasticMem, 2603.10600, 2502.01562; no trajectory-domain replication of the 2608.12218 reliance effect, so P7 stands as open. Reported as empty where empty, which supports but does not by itself establish novelty; the residual novelty risk is not a scoop but the overlap with SESA + Skill0.5 + 2608.14036 taken together.
